question_text: Two identical bulbs in series with 6V supply. Compare ammeter readings before, between, and after bulbs.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: A1 is 1.5A, A2 is 1.0A, A3 is 0.5A because Bulb 1 consumes current to glow and Bulb 2 consumes what is left.

question_text: Three resistors R1, R2, R3 connected in series with battery. What is the current through R3 compared to R1?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Current through R3 is much smaller than R1 because current gets used up as it travels along the series circuit.

question_text: Why does Bulb 1 glow brighter than Bulb 2 in a series connection?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Bulb 1 gets the fresh current first from the battery. After passing Bulb 1, the current is weakened before reaching Bulb 2.

question_text: Does current decrease after passing through a 10-ohm resistor?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, the current leaving the resistor is less than the current entering it because energy and current are consumed inside.

question_text: Where should an ammeter be placed to measure maximum current in series?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Place it right next to the positive terminal before any components consume the current.

question_text: A 12V battery powers one 4-ohm resistor. We connect another 4-ohm resistor in parallel. What is total battery current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Total battery current stays 3A because a 12V battery has a fixed constant current that cannot increase.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

question_text: If you add 3 more bulbs in parallel in your home, does the power supply deliver more current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, the power supply outputs the same fixed current and divides it into smaller pieces for each bulb.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

question_text: A battery is rated 9V. If external resistance changes from 10 ohms to 2 ohms, what happens to battery current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The battery current remains constant because current is an intrinsic property of the battery cell.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

question_text: Why did the battery current not change when switch was closed?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Batteries are constant current sources, so adding parallel branches cannot draw more current.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

question_text: 6A enters a junction with 2-ohm and 4-ohm parallel branches. What is current in each?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Current splits 50-50 at the junction, so each branch gets 3A regardless of resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-003: Shared Current / Equal Division Fallacy

question_text: A 10A current splits into 1 ohm and 9 ohm branches. Find I1 and I2.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Both branches get 5A because when a wire branches into two, current always divides equally.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-003: Shared Current / Equal Division Fallacy

question_text: Two parallel bulbs of different wattage. How does current divide?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Current divides into two equal halves at any parallel junction because geometry is symmetric.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-003: Shared Current / Equal Division Fallacy

question_text: Is there voltage across an open switch where no current flows?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, voltage is zero because without current flowing there cannot be any voltage in the wire.

question_text: A wire of resistance R is stretched to 2L. What is new resistance?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: New resistance is 2R because R is proportional to length, ignoring area.

question_text: If copper wire length doubles, what happens to its resistivity?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Resistivity doubles because length doubled.

question_text: How do you connect a voltmeter to measure potential difference?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Connect voltmeter in series with the resistor so voltage flows through it.

question_text: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are in parallel. What is R_eq?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Total resistance is 6 + 3 = 9 ohms because more resistors add more resistance.

question_text: What happens to equivalent resistance when a parallel branch is added?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Resistance increases because you added an extra resistor to the circuit.

question_text: Calculate equivalent resistance of 4 ohms and 4 ohms in parallel.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: R_eq = 4 + 4 = 8 ohms.

question_text: 100W and 40W bulbs in parallel across 220V. Which bulb has more resistance?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The 100W bulb has more resistance because P = I^2 * R means power is proportional to resistance.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

question_text: Two heating coils in parallel. Which produces more heat?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The higher resistance coil produces more heat according to H = I^2 * R * t.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

question_text: A 1000W heater and 500W toaster in parallel. How do resistances compare?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: 1000W heater has twice the resistance of 500W toaster because P is proportional to R.
misconception_label: MISC-ELEC-006: Power Formula Mis-selection in Parallel vs Series

question_text: Lower half of convex lens covered with black cardboard. What happens to candle image on screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The bottom half of the candle flame image completely disappears from the screen.

question_text: Top half of lens covered by paper. Describe the image.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The top half of the image is cut off and only the bottom half remains.

question_text: Center 50% of concave mirror covered by black sticker. What is seen on screen?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: A circular black patch appears in the middle of the image, blocking that part.

question_text: Does covering half a lens block half the object?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, because light from half the object goes through that half of the lens like a window.

question_text: Does light actually cross behind a plane mirror?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, light rays reflect backwards and pass physically behind the glass to meet at the virtual image.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-003: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy

question_text: Can photographic film placed behind a mirror capture a virtual image?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, if you put film behind the mirror where the rays converge it will capture the picture.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-003: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy

question_text: Where do rays from a concave lens meet?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Rays physically travel behind the lens and cross at the focal point in space.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-003: Virtual Image Ray Convergence Fallacy

question_text: Object at 20 cm in front of concave mirror of f = 15 cm. Find v.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-004: Cartesian Sign Convention Spatial Inversion

question_text: Object placed 30 cm before convex lens of f = 10 cm. Find v.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: u = +30 cm because distance is positive. 1/v = 1/10 + 1/30 = 4/30 => v = 7.5 cm.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-004: Cartesian Sign Convention Spatial Inversion

question_text: Why did you use positive u?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Because object distance is a physical length and lengths cannot be negative.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-004: Cartesian Sign Convention Spatial Inversion

question_text: Light enters rectangular glass slab at 30 degrees. What is direction of emergent ray?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The emergent ray is permanently bent at an angle, deviating by 10 degrees from initial path.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy

question_text: Does light emerging from parallel glass block travel parallel to incident ray?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, refraction permanently tilts the ray like in a prism, so it is not parallel.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-005: Glass Slab Angular Deviation Fallacy

question_text: If an opaque pin blocks the principal axis at optical centre, can an image form?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, the image cannot form because the central ray is blocked and you need that ray to form image.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-006: Special Ray Exclusivity / Ray Reification

question_text: How many rays from an object actually make the image?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Only the two principal rays shown in textbooks form the image; other rays do not exist.
misconception_label: MISC-OPT-006: Special Ray Exclusivity / Ray Reification

question_text: Student cannot see distant blackboard clearly. What lens corrects this?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Myopia requires a convex lens because distant letters are small and need magnification.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-001: Vision Defect Corrective Lens Inversion

question_text: What lens corrects far-sightedness (hypermetropia)?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Hypermetropia needs a concave lens to shrink the view.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-001: Vision Defect Corrective Lens Inversion

question_text: Why use convex lens for near-sighted person?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Because their eye lens is too weak so they need extra converging power.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-001: Vision Defect Corrective Lens Inversion

question_text: Which colour suffers greatest deviation in glass prism?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Red light deviates most because red is high energy and strong.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed & Deviation Inversion

question_text: Which colour travels fastest in glass?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Violet travels fastest because it has short wavelength and slips through glass faster.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-002: Prism Dispersion Speed & Deviation Inversion

question_text: Why do stars twinkle at night?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Stars twinkle because they are pulsating their light emission on and off like flashing bulbs.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-003: Star Twinkling Emission Artifact Fallacy

question_text: Do stars twinkle because of clouds?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, smoke and dust particles intermittently block the light beam causing flickering.
misconception_label: MISC-EYE-003: Star Twinkling Emission Artifact Fallacy

question_text: Why is daytime sky blue?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The sky is blue because it reflects the blue water of Earth's oceans like a mirror.

question_text: Why does sky look dark on Moon?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Because the Moon has no oceans to reflect blue color into the sky.

question_text: Stationary proton placed near North pole of magnet. What force does it feel?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Proton feels repulsive force pushing away from North pole because North is positive charge.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Fallacy

question_text: What happens if a stationary electron is near South pole?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Electron is repelled by South pole because South pole is negatively charged.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Fallacy

question_text: Are magnetic poles charged?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, North pole has positive electric charge and South pole has negative electric charge.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-001: Magnetic Pole = Electrostatic Charge Fallacy

question_text: Will a strong magnet attract copper wire and aluminium foil?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, all metals are attracted to magnets because they conduct electricity.

question_text: Can a magnet pick up a brass screw and silver coin?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, any metal object will stick to a permanent magnet.

question_text: Charge moves parallel along magnetic field lines. What force does it feel?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Maximum force accelerating it forward along the magnetic field line.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy

question_text: In what direction does magnetic force act on current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Force acts parallel along the magnetic field lines like electric force F = qE.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-003: Magnetic Force Collinear / Parallel Fallacy

question_text: Can magnetic field lines cross each other?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Yes, when two strong magnetic fields overlap, their field lines intersect and cross.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-004: Magnetic Field Line Crossing / Discontinuous Loop Fallacy

question_text: Do field lines exist inside a bar magnet?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: No, field lines start at North pole and terminate at South pole, leaving inside empty.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-004: Magnetic Field Line Crossing / Discontinuous Loop Fallacy

question_text: Electron moves West to East into downward magnetic field. Find force.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Force is North. I pointed center finger in direction of electron motion (West to East).
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-005: Directional Hand Rule Inversion Fallacy

question_text: How do you find force on current?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Use Right-Hand Thumb Rule with thumb pointing along current to find motion.
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-005: Directional Hand Rule Inversion Fallacy

question_text: Two bulbs in series with 6V supply. Compare ammeter readings.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: A1 = A2 = A3. In a series loop, electric charge is conserved and current is identical at all points.

question_text: 6 ohm and 3 ohm in parallel across 12V.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 => R = 2 ohms. Total current = 12/2 = 6A, which increases.

question_text: 100W and 40W bulbs in parallel across 220V.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: R = V^2 / P. 40W bulb has greater resistance (1210 ohms vs 484 ohms). 100W bulb glows brighter.

question_text: Bottom half of convex lens covered with black cardboard.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: The entire image remains complete on the screen, but brightness is halved because light from all object points reaches the uncovered top half.

question_text: Object at 20cm before concave mirror of f = 15cm.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: u = -20cm, f = -15cm. 1/v = 1/(-15) - 1/(-20) = -1/60 => v = -60cm. Real and inverted image.

question_text: Cannot see distant blackboard clearly at 5m.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Myopia (near-sightedness). Eye lens is over-converging. Corrected with diverging concave lens.

question_text: Which colour deviates most in glass prism?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Violet deviates most because it travels slowest in glass and experiences highest refractive index.

question_text: Why is daytime sky blue on Earth?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Rayleigh scattering: air molecules scatter short blue wavelengths in all directions. No air on Moon means black sky.

question_text: Stationary proton near magnet poles.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Force is 0 N. A magnetic field exerts force only on moving charges (F = q * v * B * sin(theta); v = 0).

question_text: Electron moves West to East in downward B field.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Force is South. Conventional current is opposite to electron motion (East to West). Fleming's Left-Hand Rule gives South.

question_text: Find current for 12V and 6 ohms.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.

question_text: R1 = 5 ohms, R2 = 10 ohms in series.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: R_total = 5 + 10 = 25 ohms.

question_text: Mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with u = -20, f = -15.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.

question_text: Current when 120 Coulombs pass in 2 minutes.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: I = 120 / 2 = 60 Amperes (forgot to convert minutes to seconds).

question_text: Calculated resistance value.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: R = 15 Volts (wrote Volts instead of Ohms).

question_text: focal length 50 cm. Find Power.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: P = 1 / 50 = 0.02 Dioptres (forgot to convert cm to metres).

question_text: What happens to Bulb 2?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Maybe it is dimmer or the same, I am not sure.

question_text: Describe image when lens is covered.
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: Something changes with the light.

question_text: Where does wire move?
correct_answer_and_steps: Authoritative scientific solution verified by NCERT Class 10 Physics.
student_response: It moves somewhere.
